articles.title: Sarvam clarifies AI strategy amid debate over hosting Chinese models
articles.summary: Co-founder Pratyush Kumar contends that a model’s country of origin and the location of the infrastructure on which it runs are two different matters. Building inference infrastructure does not take away from Sarvam’s core focus on developing its own models, he says.

articles.title: The Bull Case for Britain
articles.summary: When it comes to the UK economy, the prevailing mood has been decidedly downbeat. But Morgan Stanley’s Chief UK Economist, Bruna Skarica, sees reasons to be more optimistic — from improving productivity and the potential benefits of AI adoption to signs of resilience among UK households and businesses. In this episode, Skarica joins host Merryn Somerset Webb to make the case for a more constructive outlook. They discuss the UK’s fiscal risks, what’s driving the recent improvement in productivity, whether AI could ultimately translate into higher wages and living standards and what a stronger economy could mean for UK markets over the next five years. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Meta to price Muse Charm gadget at $300: The Information
articles.summary: The device that carries the viral Muse AI agent into the real world was unveiled in September by chief executive Mark Zuckerberg during the company's annual conference. Muse Charm underscores Meta's broader push to reduce its reliance on Apple and Google's operating systems by building its own AI platform.

articles.title: Trump administration weighs forcing US firms to disclose Chinese AI use
articles.summary: The Treasury Department and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) have discussed the plan, which would apply to companies such as Airbnb, the people said. The company uses Qwen, an AI model made by China's Alibaba , to power its AI customer service agent.
